meaning: to avoid talking about the main subject directly, often because it is uncomfortable
literal_translation: ходити навколо та около, уникаючи головного
example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what the test results said.
origin: Possibly from hunting, when beaters struck bushes to flush out birds rather than approaching them directly; the exact origin is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to hunt small animals in a thicket
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This takes the words literally; the idiom has nothing to do with hunting or animals.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to hit a plant to make it grow faster
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This misreads the words; the idiom refers to speech, not gardening.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to be very direct and honest about a difficult issue
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which describes avoiding the real subject.

explanation: 'Beat around the bush' means to avoid the main point and speak indirectly. It is used when someone delays getting to the real issue, often out of hesitation or discomfort.
